title: ipfs mcp configuration file (--mcp-config)
description: Configuration read only by `ipfs mcp` (never a Kubo repo config key). The file is named with `ipfs mcp --mcp-config=<path>` or the IPFS_MCP_CONFIG environment variable; the root `--config`/`--config-file` flag keeps its Kubo meaning (the repo config file) and is not this file. Without either, no file is read and every key takes its default. Every key carries default, offSwitch and ownerChange annotations; docs/mcp/config-reference.md is generated from them. Credentials are never literals: they are SecretRef objects naming an environment variable or an absolute file path. No key has a default network endpoint. An absent Secret file or token environment variable named by any SecretRef is never fatal, with one exception: startup proceeds with a warning and only the dependent feature is disabled (the principal whose credential reference does not resolve authenticates nothing; the agent backend whose key reference does not resolve answers backend_not_configured) until the reference resolves (CRITICAL-2, ADR-0009 section 1). The exception: ipfs mcp --http with configured principals none of which resolves a credential, and no --auth-token-* operator token, exits at start instead of serving 403 (S5).

enabled.offSwitch: false (default): no listener is opened; stdio only.

listen.offSwitch: Used only when http.enabled is true. Reserved ports of other local services are rejected.

allowed_origins.offSwitch: Empty (default): every cross-origin request to /mcp is rejected.

max_body_bytes.offSwitch: Always enforced; lower it to reject larger requests.

session_timeout.offSwitch: Idle sessions end after this duration.

http.offSwitch: Omit the section or leave http.enabled false.

groups.offSwitch: Remove a group to disable it. Destructive-class tools are excluded by default; add the selector destructive to enable them (still confirmed per call).

read_only.offSwitch: true: only confirmation-class none tools are offered.

disabled.offSwitch: List a tool name to disable that tool.

app_views.offSwitch: false: no ui:// resource is registered and no tool carries _meta.ui; every tool is still offered and returns the same result. With true, a view is served only while at least one of its linked tools is registered (ADR-0007 section 5).

tools.offSwitch: Omit for the default tool set (all groups, no destructive tools).

trusted_peers.description: Peer IDs whose peer-supplied data (addresses, and any other peer-reported string a tool returns) is returned as trusted: the untrusted marker on their entries in swarm_peers, routing_findpeer and routing_findprovs results is false. Trust is by peer ID because libp2p authenticates peer IDs; agent versions are self-reported and are never a trust signal. Entries for every other peer are marked untrusted, and the result carries the untrusted-content meta flag. The node's own data (ipfs_node_info) is not peer-supplied. A listed peer's addresses returned by routing (routing_findpeer, routing_findprovs) may still have been relayed by other DHT nodes. Not used by WebMCP, where every peer-supplied entry is untrusted.
trusted_peers.offSwitch: Empty list (the default): every peer-supplied address is marked untrusted.

name.offSwitch: Remove the principal entry: its credential then authenticates nothing.

kind.description: admin (ADR-0009 section 3) is scoped to the runtime settings route only: settings read and write, no tool access. An admin token is refused on /mcp, /agui and /a2a, and a tool principal's token is refused on the settings route (path-scoped authorization). The tool-group keys (groups, write_groups, destructive_groups, egress_ack, shell_capable, check, uar) grant an admin principal nothing and are ignored for it. The settings route is mounted only when an admin principal is configured and agent.settings.enabled is not false.

credential.offSwitch: Remove the principal entry, or remove the env variable or file it names: an unknown token gets 401. If the named environment variable or file is absent, only that principal is disabled and the start logs a warning, as long as at least one other principal (or a --auth-token-* operator token) resolves; the disabled principal authenticates nothing until the reference resolves (CRITICAL-2). If none of the configured principals resolves and no operator token is given, ipfs mcp --http exits at start naming the missing variables or files.

groups.offSwitch: List fewer groups; an empty list grants no tool. Read-class tools only.

destructive_groups.offSwitch: Empty (default): no destructive-class tool (pin_rm, mfs_rm, key_rm, repo_gc) is offered to the principal (ADR-0003 section 2).

egress_ack.offSwitch: Empty (default): every contentEgress tool is refused to this principal with egress_not_acknowledged.

shell_capable.offSwitch: Operator assertion. Under confirmation.cli a write principal needs false, otherwise its write and destructive grants are refused.

check.offSwitch: verify (default) fails closed when UAR settings are unreadable; assert records the operator's own verification. Only used for kind uar.

card_url.offSwitch: Remove the uar block: no check-uar connection is made.

admin_credential.offSwitch: null (default): settings cannot be read, so check verify fails closed. Sent to UAR as the X-UAR-Admin-Key header (not as a bearer), only to the settings path under the card URL's base, over https or to loopback.

min_version.offSwitch: null (default): the version pinned by the shipped UAR profile applies.

uar.offSwitch: null (default); required only for kind uar.

subjects.description: The OpenID Connect `sub` values (Kratos identity IDs) that resolve to this principal when auth.oidc.enabled is true (ADR-0013 section 4). Matched exactly against `sub`; the `email` claim never selects or grants a principal. A principal needs `credential`, `subjects`, or both; `credential` is optional when `subjects` has at least one entry. One subject may be listed in a `ui` principal and an `admin` principal (one person, two capabilities); each request resolves to the principal whose kind the route accepts. Two principals of the same kind listing the same subject is a configuration error at load: JSON Schema cannot compare items, so mcp/contract/agentic_test.go (TestConfigSemanticInvalidExamplesFail) pins the rule. Honored for kinds ui, human-mcp and admin only.
subjects.offSwitch: Empty (default): no subject resolves to this principal, so a session token cannot select it. Static `credential` bearers are unaffected. With auth.oidc.enabled false, subjects authenticate nothing; the subject rules are still validated at load, and a config whose only principals are session-only fails startup.

require_amr.description: Authentication methods (the `amr` claim, filled by Kratos from the session's methods) of which at least one must be present for a session identity of this principal. null (default) applies the kind default: `admin` needs any of totp, webauthn, passkey and lookup_secret; other kinds need none. A failing request gets 403 `step_up_required`. An explicit empty list accepts any `amr` including password-only sessions on an admin entry, a documented weakening (ADR-0013 section 5). Applies to JWT identities only, never to static bearers.
require_amr.offSwitch: [] accepts any `amr` (documented weakening for an admin entry). null (default) is the kind default. With auth.oidc.enabled false the key is ignored.

max_auth_age.description: Maximum age of the sign-in, `now - auth_time`, for a session identity of this principal. null (default) applies the kind default: `admin` 1h; other kinds no limit. A token without `auth_time` fails the check where it applies. A failing request gets 403 `step_up_required`. Applies to JWT identities only, never to static bearers.
max_auth_age.offSwitch: null (default) is the kind default (1h for admin, none for other kinds). A long duration weakens the bound; there is no value that disables it for admin short of a very large duration. With auth.oidc.enabled false the key is ignored.

principals.offSwitch: Empty (default): no ui, a2a, uar or admin principal exists, HTTP has no authenticated principal and the settings route is not mounted (404). A loopback listener with no principal and no operator token configured at all serves every request as the anonymous-loopback principal, which is read-only (confirmation class none tools only; no write or destructive group can be granted to it). A non-loopback listener without a verifier is refused. When principals are configured but none of them has a credential that resolves (and no --auth-token-* operator token is given), startup fails and names the principals and the environment variables or files it expected; it does not fall back to the anonymous listener. When some resolve, only those are enabled.

enabled.offSwitch: false (default): no JWT is accepted anywhere, no JWKS is fetched, GET /auth/session is not mounted (404) and only static bearer tokens authenticate, exactly as before.
enabled.description: Turns on OpenID Connect ID-token authentication for session identities forwarded by the console gateway (ADR-0013 section 4). Needs issuer, audiences and jwks_url. Static bearers are tried first and are matched exactly as without it.

issuer.offSwitch: Leave auth.oidc.enabled false: the issuer is not read. There is no built-in issuer anywhere in kubo.
issuer.description: Exact `iss` value a token must carry. Required when enabled is true; null (default) means unset.

audiences.offSwitch: Leave auth.oidc.enabled false: audiences are not read. When enabled it must list at least one value.
audiences.description: `aud` must contain at least one of these values. Required and non-empty when enabled is true.

jwks_url.offSwitch: Leave auth.oidc.enabled false: nothing is fetched. This is the one new outbound endpoint and it is configured, never derived. An unreachable URL never stops startup; JWT requests get 401 until keys load.
jwks_url.description: URL of the issuer's JSON Web Key Set. `https` only, except `http` for a loopback host (127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1]). Required when enabled is true; null (default) means unset. Fetched only when enabled.

algorithms.offSwitch: Narrow the list. `none` and `HS*` are not accepted by the schema; there is no value that switches signature checking off.
algorithms.description: Allowed JWS `alg` values. Asymmetric algorithms only: `none` and every `HS*` value are rejected.

clock_skew.offSwitch: 0s: no leeway for exp, nbf and iat.
clock_skew.description: Leeway applied to `exp`, `nbf` and `iat`. At most 2m (enforced when the configuration is loaded).

jwks_cache_ttl.offSwitch: Always enforced when enabled; lower it to refresh keys sooner. An unknown `kid` never causes more than one refetch per 30 s. Ignored when auth.oidc.enabled is false (nothing is cached or fetched).
jwks_cache_ttl.description: How long a fetched key set is cached. An unknown `kid` triggers at most one refetch per 30 s.

jwks_max_stale.offSwitch: No value removes the cap; turn the verifier off with `auth.oidc.enabled: false`. `0` and any value shorter than auth.oidc.jwks_cache_ttl fail config loading. A larger value keeps held keys usable longer while the issuer is unreachable.
jwks_max_stale.description: Longest time since the last successful key-set fetch during which a held key still verifies tokens. Past it, every JWT gets 401 until a fetch succeeds, the expiry is logged once per stale period, and static bearers are unaffected. Must be at least auth.oidc.jwks_cache_ttl (enforced when the configuration is loaded, whether or not enabled is true). Default 24h (operator ruling, 2026-10-20).

routes.offSwitch: `[]` accepts a JWT on no route, including /auth/session. The default `["session"]` accepts a JWT only on /auth/session; every other route must be listed explicitly. The earlier default is restored with `["agui","settings","index","session"]`.
routes.description: Routes that accept a JWT identity. A JWT on any other route gets 401. When the list names a route other than `session` and agent.origin_allowlist is empty, startup logs one Warn line naming both keys and continues (auth.oidc.require_origin already fails closed). Default narrowed from `["agui","settings","index","session"]` to `["session"]` by mcp-oidc-hardening.

require_origin.offSwitch: false turns the check off: a JWT identity then follows the same Origin behaviour as a static bearer. Leave true behind a shared-site gateway (ADR-0013 section 7).
require_origin.description: For a JWT identity and a method other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS, `Origin` must be present and listed in agent.origin_allowlist, otherwise 403. A request with no Origin fails. Static bearer requests keep their existing Origin behaviour.

oidc.description: OpenID Connect ID-token authentication for the console session (ADR-0013). Off unless enabled is true.
oidc.offSwitch: Omit the section or leave enabled false (default): no JWT is accepted, no JWKS is fetched, GET /auth/session answers 404, and static bearers authenticate as before.

auth.offSwitch: Omit the section (default): no session authentication of any kind.

kind.offSwitch: Leave unset or set openai: the backend is an OpenAI-compatible server and nothing contacts a UAR instance. Remove the llm section for no backend at all; make build GOTAGS=noagent removes the code. kind uar is accepted only while mcp/contract/agentic/uar-preflight.json pins a published UAR release.

agent_id.offSwitch: Read only when llm.kind is uar; set llm.kind back to openai. Must be unique per node on a shared UAR (the default collides across nodes): an agent with the same id is overwritten, system prompt included. Kubo binds and unbinds only skills it bound itself.

provider.offSwitch: Read only when llm.kind is uar; required for llm.kind uar unless llm.model is written as provider/model (resolve and settings writes refuse a uar backend with neither); set llm.kind back to openai to drop it.

mcp_name.offSwitch: Read only when llm.kind is uar and mcp_principal is set; unset mcp_principal and the agent is created without a kubo MCP binding.

mcp_principal.offSwitch: Required when llm.kind is uar (with mcp_credential_revision); null only while llm.kind is openai. UAR v1.1.0 resolves an empty tool allowlist to automatic selection and would expose the instance's native tools, so a uar backend without it is refused rather than created without a kubo binding. Names a principal of kind uar in principals; its credential is the static bearer sent to UAR with each run as the grant, never stored there. Plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless the host is listed in embeddings.insecure_http_hosts. Set llm.kind back to openai to turn the UAR backend off.

mcp_credential_revision.offSwitch: Required with llm.kind uar, as for mcp_principal (the credential_revision the UAR operator issued for the run grant). Set llm.kind back to openai to turn the UAR backend off.

mcp_scopes.offSwitch: Read only when llm.kind is uar (mcp_principal is required there); set llm.kind back to openai to send no run grant.

mcp_grant_ttl.offSwitch: Read only when llm.kind is uar. Advisory: sent to UAR as the grant expiry (expires_at_unix) and not enforced by ipfs mcp, because the grant is the uar principal static bearer. A leaked grant stays usable until that principal secret is rotated, whatever the value; at least 30s and at most 1h.

skills_dir.offSwitch: null (default): no skill is uploaded or bound by kubo, and it unbinds only skills it bound earlier in this process. Name a directory of agentskills.io skill directories (mcp/skills in a checkout) to upload each SKILL.md and bind it to the agent. A skill removed from skills_dir stays bound on UAR after a restart (kubo remembers what it bound only inside one running process). A skill of the same name already on UAR is bound only if its artifact_digest equals the digest of the local SKILL.md; a different or missing digest fails provisioning.

uar.offSwitch: null (default): every llm.uar key takes its default. The section is read only when llm.kind is uar.

base_url.offSwitch: Remove the llm section: no agent surface is mounted and no model call is made.

model.offSwitch: Remove the llm section. With llm.kind uar it names the default model of the UAR agent, and either llm.uar.provider is set or this value is written as provider/model (a uar backend with neither is refused).

api_key.offSwitch: null (default): requests carry no key (local servers). With llm.kind uar this must be a trusted-host JWT of the UAR instance, not an ordinary API key. An api_key reference whose environment variable or file is absent is never fatal: startup proceeds with a warning, only the dependent agent backend is disabled, and /agui answers 503 backend_not_configured until the reference resolves (CRITICAL-2).

llm.offSwitch: null (default): no LLM backend and no model call is ever made. /agui stays mounted whenever agent.agui is true and answers every run request 503 backend_not_configured until a backend is configured (flag, this section, or a settings write applied without restart); /a2a requires this section and is not mounted without it. The backend can appear and change at runtime through the settings API; a run in flight finishes on the backend it started with (ADR-0009 section 1).

agui.description: true mounts /agui whether or not an llm backend is configured: with no backend the route answers every run request 503 backend_not_configured (the settings page's empty state) until a backend is configured, which can happen at runtime through the settings API without a restart. Stock `ipfs mcp` keeps this flag off; Desktop's sidecar and the LKE manifest pass --agui (ADR-0009 section 8).

a2ui.description: Server-emitted A2UI surface messages on /agui (catalog discovery plus server-built surfaces, D15). Defaults on wherever /agui is on; it is a separate off switch so surfaces can be stopped without unmounting /agui.
a2ui.offSwitch: false: no A2UI surface message is emitted on /agui; the run stream is otherwise unchanged and the client-side ToolCallCard fallback renders. No effect when agent.agui is false.

a2a.offSwitch: false (default): /a2a and the agent card are not mounted (404).

origin_allowlist.description: Page origins allowed to call /agui from a browser. For a listed Origin, ipfs mcp answers the preflight (OPTIONS) and the POST with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing that origin (never *), Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS, Access-Control-Allow-Headers: authorization, content-type, Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Retry-After (so the browser chat can read when to retry a 503 resource_exhausted), and Vary: Origin. It never sends Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: the only credential is the bearer in the Authorization header, and cookies are not read. A request whose Origin is not listed gets 403 with no CORS headers. The allowlist grants no access by itself: the request still needs a ui principal's bearer.
origin_allowlist.offSwitch: Empty (default): every request to /agui that carries an Origin header is rejected with 403 and no CORS headers. Add webui://localhost, http://127.0.0.1:5001 or http://localhost:5001 to allow the Web UI chat.

enabled.description: Master switch for the runtime settings route. The route is mounted only when an admin principal is configured and this key is not false (ADR-0009 section 3).
enabled.offSwitch: false: the settings route is not mounted even with an admin principal configured; every request to it gets 404, nothing is written and nothing is dialed.

accept_secrets.description: Whether the settings API accepts write-only secret fields (the LLM api_key). On LKE this is false: the cloud key lives in an out-of-band Kubernetes Secret mounted as a file referenced by llm.api_key, and the page renders the key field as set on the server (ADR-0009 section 5).
accept_secrets.offSwitch: false: a settings write carrying a secret field is refused with secrets_not_accepted (403); a key is then set only by llm.api_key in this file or by the --llm-api-key-env/--llm-api-key-file flags.

dir.description: Directory holding the settings overlay, written with mode 0600 and applied atomically (write-then-rename). Effective settings resolve flags > overlay > this config file (ADR-0009 section 7). A write-only key stored through the settings API becomes a 0600 file here referenced as a SecretRef file.
dir.offSwitch: null (default): no overlay is read or written; the effective settings come from the flags and this file only, and nothing is persisted across restarts.

settings.offSwitch: Omit the section; without an admin principal the settings route is not mounted regardless of these keys.

max_steps.offSwitch: Always enforced; lower it to stop runs sooner.

loop.offSwitch: Limits always apply; the loop runs only when llm is configured.

modes.description: The out-of-band human gate for clients that cannot elicit. native is the OS presence prompt (macos-localauth on macOS, linux-polkit on Linux); desktop is a paired IPFS Desktop window and is opt-in since 2026-10-12 (the default is native only): it resolves write-class confirmations only, after Touch ID in the Desktop window, is never a presence resolver, and has no Windows support this phase; cli is `ipfs mcp confirm` on a TTY, is enabled only by naming it (here, in --confirm or IPFS_MCP_CONFIRM) or by confirmation.cli, and never approves calls from the stdio session. A mechanism the host cannot offer is skipped. Precedence: --confirm, then IPFS_MCP_CONFIRM, then this key, then the default.
modes.offSwitch: Leaving desktop out (the default) keeps the paired Desktop channel off. Empty list, --confirm=none or IPFS_MCP_CONFIRM=none: no out-of-band resolver runs. Per-call confirmation still applies: elicitation is used when the client supports it, otherwise write and destructive calls are refused with confirmation_unavailable.

resolvers.description: Narrows the resolvers that the effective modes enable. It is applied after the modes are resolved, whatever their source (--confirm, IPFS_MCP_CONFIRM, confirmation.modes or the default), so it can only make the gate stricter: a resolver runs only when its mode is enabled, the host offers it and it is listed here. Absent means all three. [] means none of desktop, macos-localauth and linux-polkit runs. cli is not in this list and is not narrowed by it; it is enabled only through modes or confirmation.cli. When the list removes every resolver the modes asked for, ipfs mcp prints a warning at start. Only macos-localauth and linux-polkit are presence resolvers and satisfy requires_native_prompt (destructive calls from the ui and a2a principals); desktop does not until a Desktop confirmation window consumes the pairing key, and cli and agui-interrupt never do.
resolvers.offSwitch: Remove a resolver to stop using it; [] stops desktop, macos-localauth and linux-polkit. With no resolver available, writes from non-eliciting principals are refused (confirmation_unavailable). Elicitation is always used for human-mcp principals whose client supports it.

cli.description: true enables the cli mode (ipfs mcp confirm) as if cli were listed in confirmation.modes; with confirmation.modes absent, it adds cli to the default modes (native). The principals[].shell_capable rule and the TTY requirement still apply, and cli never satisfies requires_native_prompt. cli never approves a confirmation opened by the stdio session (the local principal), because a stdio host cannot assert that it has no shell: a non-eliciting stdio client whose only resolver is cli gets confirmation_unavailable, and ipfs mcp warns at start. --confirm and IPFS_MCP_CONFIRM still win: when either is given, this key adds nothing. Setting false while confirmation.modes lists cli is a validation error.
cli.offSwitch: false (default): ipfs mcp confirm is refused unless cli is named in --confirm, IPFS_MCP_CONFIRM or confirmation.modes. true is for headless servers only and needs a TTY.

ttl.description: How long a confirmation stays open. It governs pending confirmations, confirmation tokens, and the expiry of the confirm channel and of ipfs mcp confirm. At least 1s, at most 10m; a value outside these bounds is a validation error (token expiry is kept in whole seconds). Expiry is denial.
ttl.offSwitch: Cannot be turned off: pending confirmations and tokens always expire, after this duration (default 120s, at least 1s, at most 10m); expiry is denial.

confirmation.offSwitch: Per-call confirmation of write and destructive tools cannot be turned off; it can only become stricter. The out-of-band human gate can: confirmation.modes [] or IPFS_MCP_CONFIRM=none, after which only eliciting clients can confirm.

wait.description: How long ipfs mcp keeps retrying at startup while the Kubo RPC API refuses connections or cannot be reached, for example a sidecar that starts before the daemon container is ready. Without --api the api file in the repo directory is read again on each attempt, so a daemon that starts later or restarts on another port is found. Retries use a bounded backoff; the first retry is logged at Warn and each later one at Info. The 60s default applies only with --http: plain stdio ipfs mcp defaults to no wait, because an MCP host has its own startup timeout. An explicit value is always honored. After this duration startup fails with the same error as without a wait. A daemon that answers with an error (an API.Authorizations refusal, an unsupported version) fails at once and is never retried. At most 10m.
wait.offSwitch: The schema default 60s is the --http default only (the annotation requires a Duration default); plain stdio has no wait unless this is set, so a daemon that is not reachable fails at once. 0s: no wait on either transport.

daemon.offSwitch: Omit the section for the transport default (60s with --http, none for stdio), or set daemon.wait to 0s to fail at once.

surreal_binary.offSwitch: Remove the embedded block: no process is started.

min_version.offSwitch: Always checked; an older binary is refused.

endpoint.offSwitch: Remove the remote block: no connection is made.

credential.description: Env or file reference to the SurrealDB credential. A value of the form user:password (the user part non-empty; the password is everything after the first colon) is sent as HTTP Basic authentication for a root or system user; any other value is sent as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer). The value is never logged.

base_url.offSwitch: Remove the embeddings section: no embedder request is made. The host must also be in the calling principal's egress_ack.

api_key.description: Env or file reference to the embedder API key, sent as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer). The value is never logged.

auto.offSwitch: false (default): nothing is indexed after ipfs_add; only ipfs_index_cid indexes.

mode.offSwitch: Remove the extractor block: no xberg process or request; only natively handled MIME types (the policy.mime_allowlist default, text/plain and text/markdown) are indexed (ADR-0011 V6).

xberg_binary.description: Absolute path to an operator-supplied xberg binary, supervised by ipfs mcp as `xberg serve` on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port; it stops when ipfs mcp exits. Kubo never downloads or bundles xberg (ADR-0011 V1).
xberg_binary.offSwitch: Remove the embedded block: no xberg process is started.

cache_dir.description: Model cache directory the operator names; pre-warm it when allow_model_downloads is false.

min_version.offSwitch: Always checked; an older binary is refused.

allow_model_downloads.description: true lets xberg download layout, OCR and transcription models from the Hugging Face Hub, an endpoint not otherwise configured. false (default) runs with downloads disabled; a file needing a missing model is extraction_failed (ADR-0011 V1).
allow_model_downloads.offSwitch: false (default): no model download is made; pre-warm the cache instead.

base_url.description: The xberg REST endpoint (POST /extract). There is no default. xberg documents no authentication, so a remote xberg must sit on a private network or behind an authenticating proxy (ADR-0011 V1). The host must also be in the calling principal's egress_ack.
base_url.offSwitch: Remove the remote block: no connection is made.

credential.description: Credential for an authenticating proxy in front of a remote xberg, sent as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer). The value is never logged.

max_bytes.offSwitch: Files larger than this are skipped too_large before any request is built.

max_text_bytes.description: Upper bound on the Markdown taken from one extraction; longer output is discarded and the file is skipped too_large (it is not truncated).
max_text_bytes.offSwitch: Always enforced; it bounds memory and the number of chunks one file can produce.

ocr.offSwitch: false (default): no OCR of images or scanned PDFs.

transcribe.offSwitch: false (default): no transcription of audio tracks.

extractor.offSwitch: null (default): no xberg process or request; only text/plain and text/markdown are indexed, as in ADR-0006.

base_url.description: Any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint with image (and, if enabled, video) input. There is no default. Media are sent as base64 data URLs inside the request, never as gateway URLs, so describing a file sends its bytes to this host; the host must also be in the calling principal's egress_ack (ADR-0011 V2, V7).
base_url.offSwitch: Remove the describer block: no description request is made.

api_key.description: Env or file reference to the describer API key, sent as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer). The value is never logged.

kinds.offSwitch: Empty list: nothing is described. Video is described only when listed.

max_output_tokens.offSwitch: Always enforced; bounds the length of one description.

image_max_bytes.offSwitch: Images larger than this are not described.

video_max_bytes.offSwitch: Videos larger than this are not described.

video_fps.offSwitch: Always applies to video: frames per second sampled for the video_url part.

max_requests_per_hour.offSwitch: 0: the describer is disabled even with base_url and model set.

describer.offSwitch: null (default): no description request; images and videos are skipped describer_not_configured unless OCR or transcription covers them.

enabled.description: Inert without an embeddings section, a configured stage and egress_ack coverage; a run always starts from a confirmed operator request, never in the background (ADR-0011 V4).
enabled.offSwitch: false: ipfs_index_bulk_start, ipfs_index_bulk_status and ipfs_index_bulk_cancel are not listed.

sources.offSwitch: Empty list: a run indexes nothing.

mfs_root.offSwitch: Narrow it to limit the MFS walk to a subtree.

max_files_per_run.description: File cap for one bulk run. It counts files tried: files seen minus already_indexed, excluding not_a_file entries; already-indexed files and directories do not consume it. A per-run max_files can only lower it.
max_files_per_run.offSwitch: Always enforced; a run stops after this many files.

max_bytes_per_run.offSwitch: Always enforced; a run stops after this many bytes.

files_per_minute.offSwitch: Always enforced; bounds the indexing rate of a run.

bulk.offSwitch: Omit the section for the default caps; set enabled false to hide the bulk tools.

enabled.description: Mounts POST /index/search and GET /index/status on the ipfs mcp HTTP listener for ui and human-mcp principals with the index group (ADR-0011 V5). Inert without --http and an embeddings section.
enabled.offSwitch: false: /index/search and /index/status answer 404 and nothing is read or dialed.

search_route.offSwitch: Omit the section; set enabled false to unmount the routes.

items.description: A host name or IPv4 address, optionally followed by :port. No scheme, no path, no wildcard, no credentials. A bare host covers every port on it; host:port covers that port only. Matching is case-insensitive and exact; ipfs-xberg.ipfs.svc does not cover ipfs-xberg.ipfs.svc.cluster.local.

insecure_http_hosts.description: Hosts that may be reached over plain http (no TLS) by the remote extractor, the describer, an embedder holding an api_key, a remote store holding a credential, and the agent model backend set through the settings API: a settings write or a Test connection probe accepts a plain http backend URL only for a loopback host (localhost or a literal loopback address; a *.localhost name does not count) or a host listed here, and changing the scheme of the backend URL needs the egress_confirmation for that host. Without an entry, plain http to a non-loopback extractor or describer, to an embedder with a key, or to a remote store with a credential is refused at startup because document bytes, media and credentials would travel unencrypted. List only in-cluster Service names on a network you control, for example ipfs-xberg.ipfs.svc:8000, ipfs-embedder.ipfs.svc:11434 and ipfs-surrealdb.ipfs.svc:8000, and keep those Services cluster-only with a NetworkPolicy. Loopback hosts need no entry. A remote store with no credential, and an embedder with no key, may use plain http without an entry; their plain-http cost (chunk text and vectors on the network) is documented in docs/mcp/embeddings.md, The cost. The entry relaxes the scheme rule only: the host must still be in the calling principal's egress_ack, and https endpoints are unaffected.
insecure_http_hosts.offSwitch: [] (default): plain http to a non-loopback extractor, describer, keyed embedder or credentialed remote store is refused.

embeddings.offSwitch: null (default): no SurrealDB process or connection, no embedder call, and the index tools report not configured.

SecretRef.description: A credential reference. Literal secret values are not accepted anywhere.

AbsolutePath.description: An absolute filesystem path. Relative paths and PATH lookups are rejected.

PeerId.description: A libp2p peer ID (base58btc 12D3KooW... or Qm..., or a CIDv1 libp2p-key), the same form as the tool contract's PeerId.

Host.description: A model or embedder host name (optionally with port) the principal's content may be sent to.

ListenAddress.description: host:port or a /ip4|/ip6|/dns*/.../tcp/<port> multiaddr. Ports reserved for other local services are rejected: 4000, 4001, 5001, 8080, 1906, 1907, 1908, 50051, 8181, 8081, 11434, 23001, 28000.
